mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the Rank IC of CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the Rank IC of UNRATE > 0.5pp and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the Rank IC of RSAFS 3-month increase and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% year-over-year signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face reduced output and potentially higher costs.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the Rank IC of INDPRO YoY < -2% and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to increased liquidity and lower borrowing costs.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 1%, or if the Rank IC of FEDFUNDS < 1% and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about consumer spending and economic growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls concurrently
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the Rank IC of the interaction (UNRATE↑ & PAYEMS↓) and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) during a monetary tightening cycle signals a mismatch between monetary policy and real economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market adjusts to the policy divergence.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the Rank IC of the interaction (HOUST↑ & FEDFUNDS > 2%) and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a high level of industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average signals robust economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased corporate earnings and investor confidence.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances when INDPRO > 12-month MA, or if the Rank IC of INDPRO > 12-month MA and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
